arxiv-2109-00586.title: Tracing the boron diffusion into a textured silicon solar cell by combining boron diffusion simulation with experimental and simulated scanning transmission electron beam induced current
arxiv-2109-00586.creator: Tobias Meyer, David A. Ehrlich, Peter Pichler, Valeriya Titova, Christoph Flathmann, Jan Schmidt, Michael Seibt
arxiv-2109-00586.description: Abstract The light absorption of [001] grown single-crystalline silicon wafers can be enhanced by chemical etching with potassium hydroxide resulting in a pyramid-like surface texture. Alongside this advantageous property in the context of solar energy conversion, the surface roughness leads to drawbacks as well, e.g. difficulties in measuring diffusion behaviour of dopants in the heterogeneous structure.

arxiv-2401-03490.title: Signature of excitonic insulators in phosphorene nanoribbons
arxiv-2401-03490.creator: A. F. P. de Oliveira, Andréia L. da Rosa, Alexandre C. Dias
arxiv-2401-03490.description: Abstract Phosphorene is a recently developed two-dimensional (2D) material that has attracted tremendous attention because of its unique anisotropic optical properties and quasi-one-dimensional (1D) excitons. We use first-principles calculations combined with the maximally localized Wannier function tight binding Hamiltonian (MLWF-TB) and Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) formalism to investigate quasiparticle effects of 2D and quasi-1D blue and black phosphorene nanoribbons.

arxiv-2403-17677.title: Onboard deep lossless and near-lossless predictive coding of hyperspectral images with line-based attention
arxiv-2403-17677.creator: Diego Valsesia, Tiziano Bianchi, and Enrico Magli
arxiv-2403-17677.description: Abstract Deep learning methods have traditionally been difficult to apply to compression of hyperspectral images onboard of spacecrafts, due to the large computational complexity needed to achieve adequate representational power, as well as the lack of suitable datasets for training and testing.

arxiv-2407-10283.title: Numbers Matter! Bringing Quantity-awareness to Retrieval Systems
arxiv-2407-10283.creator: Satya Almasian, Milena Bruseva, Michael Gertz
arxiv-2407-10283.description: Abstract Quantitative information plays a crucial role in understanding and interpreting the content of documents. Many user queries contain quantities and cannot be resolved without understanding their semantics, e.g., “car that costs less than $ 10 \$10 k”. Yet, modern search engines apply the same ranking mechanisms for both words and quantities, overlooking magnitude and unit information.

arxiv-2501-16893.title: Machine-learning semi-local exchange-correlation functionals for Kohn-Sham density functional theory of the Hubbard model
arxiv-2501-16893.creator: Eoghan Cronin 1, Rajarshi Tiwari 1,2, Stefano Sanvito 1
arxiv-2501-16893.description: Abstract The Hubbard model provides a test bed to investigate the complex behaviour arising from electron-electron interaction in strongly-correlated systems and naturally emerges as the foundation model for lattice density functional theory (DFT). Similarly to conventional DFT, lattice DFT computes the ground-state energy of a given Hubbard model, by minimising a universal energy functional of the on-site occupations.

arxiv-2503-12842.title: Heavy-tailed random vectors: theory and applications
arxiv-2503-12842.creator: Dimitrios G. Konstantinides, Charalampos D. Passalidis
arxiv-2503-12842.description: Abstract . In this paper we introduce and study several multivariate, heavy-tailed distribution classes, and we explore their closure properties and their applications. We consider the class of multivariate, positively decreasing distributions, and its intersection with other multivariate distribution classes. Next, we show that the smallest of these new classes contains the standard multivariate regular variation class.

arxiv-2507-00975.title: A high-temperature furnace for multi-modal synchrotron-based X-ray microscopy and diffraction imaging
arxiv-2507-00975.creator: Louis Lesage, Yves Watier, Helena Isern, Aditya Shukla, Virginia Sanna, Thomas Dufrane, Yubin Zhang, Carsten Detlefs, Can Yıldırım \IUCrCemaillink can.yildirim@esrf.fr
arxiv-2507-00975.description: Abstract The design, calibration, and initial application of a non-contact high-temperature furnace developed for in situ synchrotron X-ray experiments are presented. The system enables a stable operation up to 1000 °C 1000\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolCelsius} , with heating rates exceeding 6000 °C min − 1 6000\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolCelsius}\text{\,}{\mathrm{min}}^{-1} and thermal stability better than ± 2 °C \pm$2\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolCelsius}$ .

plos-pone-0012149.title: Spiroplasma Bacteria Enhance Survival of Drosophila hydei Attacked by the Parasitic Wasp Leptopilina heterotoma
plos-pone-0012149.creator: Jialei Xie, Igor Vilchez, Mariana Mateos
plos-pone-0012149.description: PLOS ONE research article. Maternally-transmitted associations between endosymbiotic bacteria and insects are ubiquitous. While many of these associations are obligate and mutually beneficial, many are facultative, and the mechanism(s) by which these microbes persist in their host lineages remain elusive.

pmc-11664477.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Levels of Non-Tuberculous Bacteria Isolates from Sputum of TB Patients in Ghana
pmc-11664477.creator: Portia Abena Morgan, Desmond Opoku Ntiamoah, Prince Asare, Ishaque Siam Mintah, Stephen Osei-Wusu, Augustine Asare Boadu, Emelia Konadu Danso, Ivy Naa Koshie Lamptey, Emmanuel Afreh, Amanda Tetteh, Adwoa Asante-Poku, Isaac Darko Otchere, Dorothy Yeboah-Manu
pmc-11664477.description: BackgroundPatients with tuberculosis (TB) often harbor diverse bacteria in their sputum, including both commensal and opportunistic pathogens. This study aimed to characterize the sputum microbiota of TB patients before and after the intensive phase of anti-TB treatment and assess changes in bacterial diversity and antibiotic resistance profiles.

pmc-11716880.title: Association Between Sleep Measures and Cognition Performance: Insights from a Digital Sleep Assessment Study
pmc-11716880.creator: Huitong Ding, Chenglin Lyu, Edward Searls, Spencer Low, Zachary T Popp, Zexu Li, Salman Rahman, Akwaugo Igwe, Kristi Ho, Phillip H Hwang, Ileana De Anda‐Duran, Robert J Thomas, Vijaya B. Kolachalama, Rhoda Au, Honghuang Lin
pmc-11716880.description: BackgroundSleep disorders as a contributing factor to cognitive impairment have spurred growing interest. The advent of digital technology facilitates the collection of comprehensive sleep measures in a home setting. The objective of this study is to examine the association between digital sleep measures and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA).

pmc-12597006.description: Vibrio alginolyticus and Vibrio parahaemolyticus pose significant threats to various marine fish species, with mortality rates reaching as high as 90 %. Outer membrane proteins represent promising antigens for creating immune responses. pmc-13405498.title: Exploring the Dermocosmetic Value of Synthetic Aminopyrimidine-Thioethers
pmc-13405498.creator: Inês C. C. Costa, Joana Silva, Isabel Oliveira Abreu, Juliana Antunes Gaspar, Susete Pinteus, Celso Alves, Maria L. S. Cristiano, Rui Pedrosa
pmc-13405498.description: Skin functionalities are instrumental in four main domains: protection, regulation, sensation, and support. However, excessive exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation can compromise skin integrity and, in turn, affect its functions, by generating reactive oxygen species (ROS). Aiming to protect skin from UV radiation, sunscreens incorporate UV filters and antioxidants that absorb/reflect UV rays and neutralise free radicals, respectively.

pmc-13565688.title: Surgical Management of Extensive Urine Extravasation Resulting in Urethrocutaneous Fistulation and Soft Tissue Necrosis of the Femoral Region Secondary to Pelvic Urethral Rupture in Two Cats
pmc-13565688.creator: Dongwoo Kim, Gyeong-Jin Koo, Sang-Kwon Lee, Yoonhoi Koo, Min Jang, Sung-Ho Yun, Young-Sam Kwon, Jinsu Kang
pmc-13565688.description: Simple SummaryPelvic urethral rupture is a serious injury in cats that can cause urine to leak into the surrounding tissues. When urine spreads into the hindlimb region, it can damage the skin and underlying soft tissues, leading to tissue death and the formation of abnormal openings through which urine drains. This report describes two young cats with this uncommon complication.
